Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How does squinting your eyes work? Specifically when you are looking at something and without closing your eyelids, blur your vision?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your eyes are like little cameras. When you squint, you make your eyes really small, kind of like pinching them together but not all the way shut.

When your eyes are open wide, lots of light goes in and your brain gets a clear picture. But when you squint, only a tiny bit of light comes in. This makes the picture a little fuzzy or blurry, like when you look through a tiny keyhole.

Squinting helps your eyes block out some of the extra light and helps you see things a little better when the sun is really bright or when something is hard to see. But because less light comes in, everything looks a little blurry, not super sharp.

So, squinting is like putting on tiny sunglasses with your own hands! But it makes things look a little fuzzy because you’re letting in less light.
